newsitem.title: USA: IRS is broadening probe of "yield buring" - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: IRS is broadening probe of "yield buring" - WSJ.

text.p: The Internal Revenue Service has expanded its investigation into municipal bond "yield burning" in an effort to recover money from dozens of municipalities, The Wall Street Journal said.

In Thursday's electronic edition, the paper quoted IRS municipal bond enforcement head Marcus Owens, who said the agency is now investigating 36 cases of suspected yield burning, up from about six just weeks ago.
Owens told The Journal he expects the number of cases to grow in the months ahead.
The IRS probe began in 1994, the paper said.
Between 1990 and 1993, the paper said, municipalities issued more than $200 billion in municipal bonds for advanced refundings, the paper said.
To complete these transactions, the paper said, Wall Street firms handling the refundings had to create special escrow accounts composed of Treasury securities.
Federal regulators have been examining whether the firms improperly inflated prices of the escrow bonds by "burning" down the yields on these securities, the paper said.
